findings.text: The method ran, installed or downloaded the package it checks, against its own red line (python -c "import …", dotnet add package, mvn dependency:resolve, go mod download, require and importlib, and a gate running npm ci and pip install before any name was checked). Every such order is replaced by read-only checks and the wrapper's recipes; the gate checks names first and installs without lifecycle scripts; a red line is added after line 395, which stays byte-identical (changes 1a-1h).

Two mechanisms were described as running: loading on a phrase match (tests/skill-loading.test.js records nothing loads a specialist that way) and the refinement-loop letter (docs/REFINEMENT_LOOP.md: "the loop is **NOT RUNNING** today"). The text is fenced as a design and every string tests/critic-warnings-are-critical.test.js pins survives (changes 2a-2d).

Names the file called invented are registered (email-validator-pro on npm since 2017, serde_json_ext on crates.io, commons-security under three other Maven groups); react-query still installs; pgvector's extension is named vector; the huggingface_hub[cli] extra and react-codeshift are stale (changes 3a-3d, 1c).

The headline statistics were unsourced or stale ("dominant", "within hours", "commercial frontier models", "roughly"), and the file lacked the reason existence alone proves nothing, the four confusion classes and dependency confusion (change 4).

The existence tests and signature checks were refuted, misattributed or could not tell names apart: npm view answers for placeholders; PyPI's Trusted Publishing and attestations were conflated; NuGet and Maven signatures exist on every package; cargo search is textual; the Postgres view answers only for the server queried. Two statements contradicted the wrapper and now agree with it (changes 5a, 5b).

Stale and refuted commands: the renamed .NET vulnerability command, the attestation label, cargo search's textual matching, the crates.io user-agent and rate rule, and the Rust hyphen rule (changes 6a-6d).

The Output Format held illustrative counts that could be copied as data, "Critical" as a confidence, an unchecked DepScope claim and an unsourced slopcheck invocation, and contradicted the wrapper. Replaced by a pointer to the wrapper's response format (change 7).
The confidence rule (one technique means LOW) contradicted the wrapper, which rates a registry answer or declaration files lacking the member as HIGH on its own (change 8; completed by leftover 2).

REFIND and MetaRAG were called state of the art for catching fabricated citations, which their abstracts do not say; "100% precision on semantic errors" generalised one small Python study (changes 9a, 9b).

"C and C++ have no centralized package registry" is wrong as an absolute: ConanCenter and the vcpkg curated registry are central catalogues. The sentence is corrected; checked C and C++ examples are carried to round 2 (change 10).
The Go example's heading said "wrong import subpath inside real module"; the real code is a separate module (change 11).
Three Postgres verification comments drew the wrong conclusion ("empty = hallucinated"; \dx+ lists actual functions; pg_am lists valid access methods) (changes 12a-12d).
"Fabricated citations are common in AI-generated security claims" had no source, and the vulnerability lookup had no address (change 13).
The Django example lacked the real function, and the huggingface example lacked today's status; carried by change 1a, both confirmed by the session's raw probes.
The node-fetch row sat under "Hallucinated" although node-fetch is a real package, and gave no version (change 15).
Red line 391 demanded a signature check that proves nothing on registries where every package is signed (change 16).

Two field terms were missing from the trigger vocabulary: "package hallucination" and "library hallucination"; the list only grows, and no corpus prompt contains either phrase, so the match rate is unaffected (change 17). "package confusion" is deliberately not added.
